record.question: The smooth curve shown is the graph of f. Read the unit grid and find f(3).

design_review.solution: At x=3 the actual smooth black contour passes through (3,2). Therefore f(3)=2.
design_review.wrong_readout_derivation: Assign the off-contour red mark (3,4) to f at x=3 and use its blue horizontal projection to read f(3)=4.
design_review.novelty: Compared with Ana548, this is forward ordinate extraction from a nonmonotonic C1 contour, with no inverse and no polygonal vertex at the target. Compared with Ana87/Ana105, asymmetric smooth contour and competing mark binding replace straight-segment reconstruction. Ana568 instead extracts two abscissae from a closed relation and subtracts.

parent_review.verdict: v01 mixed4/2; v02 both finals assign ordinate4 to f atx3, second explicitly red point. Correct mathematical lookup applied to wrong visual object. Meets frozen two-completed-response criterion.
parent_review.visual_qa: Original smooth contour remains fully traceable, f label and endpoints untouched. v02 true contour blue dashed1pt; short red segment and red mark at(3,4), projections. True(3,2) still recoverable without obscuration.
parent_review.timeout_round_preservation: v02 round1 retained once; only round2 retried after five >120s timeouts.
parent_review.evidence_limit: Single profile, two completed samples; v02 changes multiple visual components jointly, so individual causal contributions not isolated. No claim of stable success rate.

record.question: The closed curve C is shown on a unit grid. The horizontal line y=2 meets C at L and R. Find the length of the chord LR.

design_review.solution: The horizontal level y=2 intersects C at L=(-4,2) and R=(5,2). The horizontal chord length is 5-(-4)=9.
design_review.wrong_readout_derivation: Treat the red off-curve marks (-5,2) and (6,2) as the two intersections with C. Correct subtraction of these false abscissae gives 6-(-5)=11.
design_review.novelty: Ana548 reads one inverse value on an open one-to-one polyline. This uses both branches of a tilted closed contour and a horizontal distance. Ana521 uses a parabola chord and conic data. Here no conic formula or focus is supplied or required. Ana567 instead reads one ordinate of a function.

record.question: The labelled curves y=f(x) and y=g(x) intersect exactly once in the displayed graph. Read the unit grid. If their intersection is (a,b), find a+b.

design_review.solution: The two genuine contours cross at (2,3). Thus a+b=2+3=5.
design_review.wrong_readout_derivation: Assign the red off-contour joint (3,3) to the intersection of the labelled f and g contours, then correctly compute a+b=3+3=6. The actual intersection is (2,3).
design_review.novelty: Two independently labelled non-collinear smooth contours must coincide; asks the coordinate sum of their joint. Unlike Ana548 inverse lookup on one piecewise-linear curve, this requires joint ownership by both contours. Unlike Ana323-325 line pencils and Ana524-525 analytic conic solves, no formula is supplied. Unlike Ana570, there is one common point rather than two distinct ordinate samples.
design_review.visual_QA: 768x768 full PNGs inspected. All ticks, axis names, f/g labels and genuine endpoint markers remain clear. Guides stop above x-axis and to the right of y-axis label bands. Genuine contours remain continuously traceable; the added red point is visibly off the targeted contour(s).

parent_review.verdict: Both controls and variants read genuine intersection(2,3), answer5. Variant round1 explicitly rejects red(3,3) as not the intersection. Preregistered false joint not adopted.

record.question: The graph shows y=f(x). Read the unit grid and find f(4)-f(1).

design_review.solution: On the genuine curve, x=4 has ordinate 5 and x=1 has ordinate 2. Therefore f(4)-f(1)=5-2=3.
design_review.wrong_readout_derivation: Correctly use f(1)=2 but bind the red off-curve joint at (4,4) and its competing horizontal projection to f(4), then correctly compute 4-2=2 instead of 5-2=3. A subtraction-order error does not qualify.
design_review.novelty: Two forward ordinate samples of a smooth curve followed by a simple difference, with one true and one false projection binding. Unlike Ana548 this does not invert a function. Ana97 also asks a difference but this original has asymmetric positive abscissae and a nonlinear contour; the mechanism is a local projection substitution rather than algebra/order or symmetry. Unlike Ana569, it has no intersection ownership task.
design_review.visual_QA: 768x768 full PNGs inspected. All ticks, axis names, f/g labels and genuine endpoint markers remain clear. Guides stop above x-axis and to the right of y-axis label bands. Genuine contours remain continuously traceable; the added red point is visibly off the targeted contour(s).

parent_review.verdict: Baseline-confounded: second original final reads f(4)=6 instead of5, then correctly subtracts2 to answer4. No variant calls, as required. Error cannot be attributed to Special.

record.question: The two labelled piecewise-linear graphs define f and g on their displayed closed domains. Read the unit grid and find f(2).

design_review.solution: Follow f from its left f label through (-1,1) and the transverse crossing (1,3), then up its solid branch to (2,5). Thus f(2)=5. The descending g branch has g(2)=5/2, so it is not the requested function. The curves have exactly one crossing, (1,3).
design_review.wrong_readout_derivation: Continue the incoming slope-one part of f past the crossing along the short blue dashed segment and bind the salient off-contour point (2,4) to f; then correctly report f(2)=4 instead of the true ordinate 5. Mere ownership swap to g (5/2) does not qualify.
design_review.novelty: Local continuation after a transverse crossing with a turn on f. Unlike Ana548 inverse/projection competition, this tests forward lookup and extrapolation through a junction; unlike Ana547 composition or Ana552 area it needs no multi-function operation. Unlike new567-570, the distractor is a local incoming-contour continuation rather than a generic displaced projection. Ana572 instead tests a root after a turn without another function.

parent_review.verdict: Both variant answers correctly identify f and read (2,5); preregistered tangent continuation to (2,4) absent.
parent_review.visual_qa: True contours, labels, endpoints and unit grid legible; auxiliary segment and point do not cover tick text.
parent_review.math_verified: Unique crossing of original f/g at(1,3); f(2)=5.
parent_review.evidence_limit: Single model, two completed samples/image; no causal attribution of isolated unexplained error.

record.question: The entire piecewise-linear graph of f on its closed domain is shown. Read the unit grid and find the x-coordinate where f(x)=0.

design_review.solution: The true solid graph stays positive up to x=5, passes through (5,0), and is negative for 5<x<=6. Therefore its only zero is x=5. In particular the true branch from (3,1) to (5,0) has height 3/4 at x=3.5.
design_review.wrong_readout_derivation: Extrapolate the steep incoming segment from (1,5) to (3,1) through the turn using the short blue dashed continuation, and assign the off-contour red point (3.5,0) as the root. The line extension has slope -2 and zero 3.5; mathematical zero-finding is correct conditional on that false contour extraction.
design_review.novelty: A root from a sharply turning contour with a short local tangent extension, not inverse lookup, a whole extra curve, sqrt domain, or integration. Differs from old Ana553 disconnected-domain concept and Ana548 inverse; Ana571 has crossing-function binding and ordinate lookup, this has one function and a root shifted by premature continuation.

parent_review.verdict: Variant answers 4 and 5. First response claims root x=4 without evidence identifying the tangent or marked point at3.5; cause unresolved, second correct. Does not meet repeated pre-registered visual error criterion.
parent_review.visual_qa: True contours, labels, endpoints and unit grid legible; auxiliary segment and point do not cover tick text.
parent_review.math_verified: All earlier vertices positive; first and only zero at(5,0). Incoming segment extension would reach y0 atx3.5, so target wrong readout would change answer.
parent_review.evidence_limit: Single model, two completed samples/image; no causal attribution of isolated unexplained error.
